Preface | the comparison below is laid out in four columns: occupation direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which choice fits better. Compliance, inspection and investigation often connect within the same institution or project, but connection does not mean they are interchangeable; when choosing across directions, the legal basis, procedure, authorization, evidence and responsibility boundaries of that direction must be learned anew.

Key difference: this occupation takes government property and contract and regulatory compliance as its object, completing basis checking, document review, on-site inspection, sampling and interviews, evidence collection and preservation, reporting, advising and testifying, and is responsible for the facts and the procedure; the other roles centre on broader compliance enforcement, building codes, environmental regulations, compliance governance systems, or occupational health and safety, and usually each has more specialised legal bases, standards, procedures and authorization requirements and does not carry primary responsibility for establishing the facts of government property and contract compliance (though it must coordinate and clearly delimit boundaries with inspection and investigation roles).

Better suited to people who are willing to check documents and sites item by item against clauses and evidence, can explain the basis and the facts clearly amid multi-party communication and challenges from the parties concerned, and push rectification and referral forward within statutory or institutional procedure and authorization boundaries.

Core work and outputs: check the basis, jurisdiction and applicable version, review records, reports and other documents to ascertain facts or find variances, inspect government property and manufactured products and contractor-held property, investigate suspected violations of licences or permits, collect and preserve evidence and send samples for testing, and write reports and recommended actions and appear in court or testify as required; the outputs are reviewable inspection or investigation reports together with evidence, rectification and recommended actions (O*NET/SOC 13-1041.04).

Better suited to people who want to work on compliance system enforcement, advice and training within an institution or industry; this occupation leans more towards specific inspection, investigation and evidence collection for government property and contracts.

Core work and outputs: identify and explain the applicable regulations and internal systems, carry out compliance reviews and training and advice and handle violation leads, and produce compliance opinions together with monitoring and rectification tracking results.
Compliance Officers (13-1041.00)

Key difference: construction and building inspectors take building codes and construction quality and safety compliance as their object, and their outputs are construction inspection records and rectification notices; this occupation takes government property and contract clauses and overall regulatory compliance as its object, and its outputs are inspection or investigation reports together with evidence and recommended actions, and it usually does not carry specialised determination responsibility for building structural safety and construction techniques (though it must coordinate with construction inspectors).

Better suited to people who want to inspect building codes and construction quality on site; this occupation leans more towards contract and regulatory compliance, investigation, evidence collection and reporting.

Core work and outputs: inspect construction quality, structures and safety facilities against building codes and drawings and record defects, issue inspection records and rectification notices and re-inspect.
Construction and Building Inspectors (47-4011.00)

Key difference: environmental compliance inspectors take environmental laws and regulations and emissions, monitoring and waste compliance as their object, and their outputs are environmental inspection, monitoring and assessment conclusions; this occupation takes government property and contract and overall regulatory compliance as its object, and its outputs are inspection or investigation reports and recommended actions, and it usually does not carry technical determination responsibility for environmental monitoring and emission compliance (though it must coordinate with environmental professionals).

Better suited to people who want to inspect environmental regulations and emissions and monitoring compliance; this occupation leans more towards government property and contract compliance, investigation and evidence.

Core work and outputs: inspect emissions, pollution control, waste and monitoring facilities against environmental regulations and check ledgers, and issue environmental inspection and monitoring conclusions and rectification requirements.
Environmental Compliance Inspectors (13-1041.01)

Better suited to people who want to work on compliance system building, risk governance and team management; this occupation leans more towards specific on-site and document inspection, investigation and evidence collection.

Core work and outputs: establish and maintain compliance systems, processes, training, monitoring and reporting mechanisms, organize risk assessments and rectification tracking and communicate externally with regulators.
Compliance Managers (11-9199.02)

Key difference: occupational health and safety specialists take workplace hazard identification and protection and occupational health compliance as their object, and their outputs are hazard assessments, protection recommendations and inspection records; this occupation takes government property and contract and overall regulatory compliance as its object, and its outputs are inspection or investigation reports together with evidence and recommended actions, and it usually does not carry technical determination responsibility for occupational hazards and occupational health monitoring (though it must coordinate with occupational health professionals).

Better suited to people who want to work on occupational hazard identification and protection and occupational health compliance; this occupation leans more towards government property and contract compliance, investigation and reporting.
Core work and outputs: identify workplace hazards, assess exposure and risk, inspect protection facilities and system implementation and prepare assessment, protection recommendations and training.
